questions.problem: Find the orthogonal projection matrix that maps $x\in {R}^{2}$ onto the subspace spanned by an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-4$ of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 \\ 4 & 4\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

Moreover, ${u}_{i}\cdot {u}_{i}^{T}$ is the projection matrix corresponding to ${u}_{i}.$

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to $\lambda =-4.$ Computing $A-(-4)I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A+4I & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 \\ 4 & 4\end{aligned}]+4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ 4 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-2{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],
$$

where $‖v‖=\sqrt{5}.$ Dividing $v$ by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: 

$$
u=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {u}^{T} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the orthogonal projection matrix that maps $x\in {R}^{2}$ onto the subspace spanned by an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2$ of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -4 & 18\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

Moreover, ${u}_{i}\cdot {u}_{i}^{T}$ is the projection matrix corresponding to ${u}_{i}.$

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to $\lambda =2.$ Computing $A-2I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -4 & 18\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ -4 & 16\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ -4 & 16\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 0 \\ -4 & 16 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=4{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],
$$

where $‖v‖=\sqrt{17}.$ Dividing $v$ by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: 

$$
u=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {u}^{T} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}[\begin{aligned}4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{17}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{17}[\begin{aligned}16 & 4 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-6,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
questions.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =(-1)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}]+(-6)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =(-1)\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}]+(-6)\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}((-1)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}]+(-6)\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}((-1)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}]+(-6)\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-25 & 10 \\ 10 & -10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-9,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
questions.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}[\begin{aligned}2 & 3\end{aligned}]+(-9)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{13}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 3\end{aligned}]+(-9)\cdot \frac{1}{13}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{13}(4\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 3\end{aligned}]+(-9)\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 2\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{13}(4\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 6 \\ 6 & 9\end{aligned}]+(-9)\cdot [\begin{aligned}9 & -6 \\ -6 & 4\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{13}[\begin{aligned}-65 & 78 \\ 78 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 6 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=8,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
questions.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}10 & 6 \\ 6 & 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
